physical_harm: Complainant’s injuries and the death of his two brothers
number_of_offences: Charged under multiple sections of IPC, but the number of counts upheld is not stated
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the evidence that the appellants were summoned under Section 319 Cr.P.C. based on the satisfaction of the Trial Court derived from the evidence on record during the trial.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses' credibility based on the evidence recorded during the trial and the satisfaction of the Trial Court, without explicitly stating the credibility of individual witnesses.
trial_duration: FIR registered on 09.06.2018; charge sheet filed but appellants not mentioned; summons ordered on 23.09.2022; High Court affirmed on 03.01.2023; Supreme Court judgment on 18.07.2023
legal_representation: S. Nagamuthu, Ram Kishor Singh Yadav, Kaushal Yadav, Nandlal Kumar Mishra, Dr. Ajay Kumar, Dr. Sushil Balwada, Vivekanand Rana, Pramod Kumar, Srilok Nath Rath, Ms. Reena Rao for the Appellants; Ratnakar Dash, Shashank Shekhar Singh, Yatharth Singh, Ms. Amrita Panda for the Respondents
investigation_status: FIR registered under Sections 147, 148, 149, 302, 452, 307, 504 of IPC; charge sheet filed but appellants not mentioned; summons ordered under Section 319 Cr.P.C.

appeal_history.high_court: Order dated 03.01.2023 affirmed the trial court order

prosecution_argument: The State argued that the summoning order under Section 319 Cr.P.C. was valid and that the appellants were properly summoned to join the trial, with the High Court affirming this order. The prosecution emphasized that the principles of natural justice and opportunity of hearing are not mandatory for persons summoned under Section 319 Cr.P.C.
defence_argument: The appellants contended that they were not given an opportunity of hearing before being summoned as accused, which violated the principles of natural justice. They argued that the Jogendra Yadav judgment mandates such a hearing and that the summoning order should be set aside.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the power under Section 319 Cr.P.C. is to proceed with the trial and not to jeopardize it, and that the principle of natural justice is not a mandatory requirement for persons summoned under Section 319 Cr.P.C.
precedent_relied_upon: Hardeep Singh vs. State of Punjab & Ors. (2014) 3 SCC 92; Brijendra Singh & Ors. v/s. State of Rajasthan (2017) 7 SCC 706; Sukhpal Singh Khair v. State of Punjab (2023) 1 SCC 289; Jogendra Yadav and Ors. vs. State of Bihar and Anr. (2015) 9 SCC 244
